security.title: Your books are nobody else's business.
security.lead: What protects your data, in plain words.

items.title: Fail-closed tenancy
items.body: Queries without an active business raise an error instead of returning everyone's rows. Another business's record answers 404.

items.title: Sessions, not tokens in the browser
items.body: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies with CSRF checks on every change, including sign-in itself.

items.title: Argon2id passwords
items.body: Memory-hard hashing, a 12 character minimum, and common passwords refused.

items.title: Rate limits everywhere
items.body: Every endpoint has a throttle, with strict ones on sign-in, sign-up and password reset, plus limits at the proxy.

items.title: Content Security Policy
items.body: A fresh nonce on every response and strict-dynamic, so injected scripts do not run.

items.title: Row locks and one lock order
items.body: Stock, numbering and balances are read and written under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, always in primary key order.

items.title: An audit trail
items.body: Every create, update, post and delete writes who, what, when and the request it came from.

items.title: Nothing leaks in errors
items.body: Unexpected errors return a request id and nothing else. The details stay in the server log.

security.report: Found a problem? Report it privately through GitHub security advisories or support@ahmershah.dev.
security.pageLead: What protects your data, in plain words, and how we prove it on every change.

items.a: Yes. It is open source under the MIT license. You can run it on your own server at no cost.

items.q: Can several businesses share one installation?
items.a: Yes. Each business has its own books, stock and staff, and the server refuses any request for another business's data.

items.q: Does it work in Urdu and Arabic?
items.a: Every screen does, with right-to-left layouts. Printed invoices in all three languages arrive with sales.
Tax arrives in milestone M5, starting with Pakistan and then the Gulf. Rates are stored as dated data, never hard-coded.

items.q: What happens if I make a mistake in a posted entry?
items.a: Posted entries never change. You post a reversal, which keeps a complete and honest audit trail.

guides.title: How to use this page
overview: This is your business at a glance. Use the menu on the left to open any part of Karobar.
New here? Start with Inventory, then Setup: add your units (piece, carton) and your shop or store room.
Then add your products, record the stock you already have, and you're ready to buy and sell.
members: Invite the people who work with you by typing their email and choosing a role.
They get an email with a link. Once they accept, they can sign in to this business.
Remove someone at any time; they lose access straight away.
roles: A role decides what a person can see and change, for example a cashier or an accountant.
Tick only what that job needs. View lets them look, Create and Update let them change, Post makes it final.
Give each member one role on the Members page.
audit: Every change anyone makes is written here: who did it, when, and what changed.
Nothing here can be edited or deleted, so you can always find out what happened.
journal: Most entries are made for you when you post a sale, purchase or stock change. Use this page for anything else, like rent paid or money you put into the business.
Press New entry, pick the accounts, and enter the amounts. The money going in (debit) must equal the money going out (credit).
Save a draft while you work, then press Post. Posted entries can't be changed; if you made a mistake, press Reverse.
chart: These are the headings your money is sorted under, like Cash, Bank, Sales and Rent. A standard list is already set up for you.
You only need to add an account if you want a new heading, for example a second bank account.
Group accounts only add up the accounts under them; you can't post to a group directly.
trialBalance: This shows the balance of every account on a date. The two totals must always be equal.
Pick a date to see how things stood then. Use Export to send it to your accountant as a spreadsheet.
ledger: Pick an account to see every entry that touched it, with the running balance.
Choose dates to look at one month or one year. Export downloads the list.
periods: Your financial year is split into months. New entries can only go into open months.
When a month's books are final, close it so nobody adds to it by mistake. You can reopen it if needed.
products: Add everything you buy or sell. Give each one a short code (SKU), a name and the unit you count it in.
If you also buy it by the carton or box, add a pack with how many pieces it holds and its barcode.
Set a reorder level and Karobar warns you when stock falls below it.
entries: Use this page to change stock by hand: receive goods, take some out, move it between stores, or correct a count.
Choose the type, the store and the date, then add the products and quantities.
Save a draft, check it, then press Post. Posting changes your stock and your books together.
onHand: This shows how much of each product you have in each store, and what it is worth at cost.
Pick a store to see only that one. The total at the top is the value of all your stock.
alerts: Products below their reorder level, and batches that expire soon, are listed here.
You also get this list by email every morning.
setup: Add the units you count in, like PCS for pieces or KG for kilograms.
Add each place you keep stock, like your shop and your store room. Every stock change needs one.

chat.notice: Your question and the figures your role can see are sent to Groq, an outside AI service, to write the answer. The assistant can prepare a draft for you to check, but nothing is saved until you press Confirm, and it never posts, pays or deletes. It can make mistakes, so check important numbers. Each message carries a signature, so any later change can be detected.

hr.idRetention: Keep national IDs of people who left for (years)
hr.idRetentionHint: At least 6 years after the tax year they left in, because tax records must be kept that long. Bank accounts are cleared 90 days after someone leaves.
hr.fillHint: Adds the country's holidays. Eid and other moon-sighted dates are estimates: check them when they are announced and change the date here. Days already on the list are kept.
hr.noHolidays: No holidays for this year yet.

payroll.title: Payroll
payroll.body: Work out a month's pay for everyone, check it, then post it. Posting books the salaries and makes the payslips.
payroll.workOutHint: Pay comes from each person's contract, with unpaid leave and absences taken off. You can work a month out again until it is posted.
payroll.noRuns: No month has been worked out yet.
payroll.draftHint: Check these figures. After posting they can't change.
payroll.postedNow: Posted. The salaries are in the books and the payslips can be printed.
payroll.changed: Pay changed since this was worked out, so the figures were updated. Check them, then post again.
payroll.slabsBody: The income tax slabs for each tax year, as the law sets them. Payroll uses the table for the month it pays.
payroll.fillHint: Fill in the official slabs that come with the app, or type a year's slabs yourself. Check them against the law before relying on them.
payroll.noTables: No tax slabs yet. Payroll needs them before it can work out income tax.
payroll.sourceHint: The law or notice, so anyone can check the figures later.
payroll.slabHint: Each slab: on yearly income above this amount, pay the fixed amount plus the rate on the part above it. The first slab starts at 0.
payroll.openingTitle: Pay before Karobar this tax year
payroll.openingHint: If payroll starts here partway through the tax year, or someone joined from another job, type the taxable salary already paid and the tax already withheld this tax year. Income tax then counts the whole year. You can't change it once the person has posted pay here this tax year.
payroll.openingNone: Nothing typed in for this tax year.
payroll.openingNotePlaceholder: July to October, from our old records
